candidates.shared: The geographic east/west imagery appears with divine sovereignty or universal recognition.
candidates.difference: Isaiah emphasizes knowing that YHWH alone is God from east to west; Q 2:115 emphasizes God's ownership of east/west and God's face wherever one turns.
candidates.caveat: Not equivalent wording or ritual orientation law; Hebrew text and variant versions need deeper comparison.

candidates.shared: Both discuss whether God has a son.
candidates.difference: John 3:16–18 describes God's unique Son as sent for salvation, whereas Qur'an 2:116 rejects the attribution of a son to God and asserts God's universal dominion.
candidates.caveat: The Qur'anic verse does not name John or Jesus in this verse; Christian sonship theology cannot be reduced to biological procreation; translation of Greek monogenēs and historical interlocutors require care.

open_questions: Confirm Hebrew text, Greek text, manuscript transmission, and critical edition for both candidates before any public promotion.
Assess whether Q2:111–113 reflects identifiable sectarian polemics rather than treating all Jewish or Christian positions as homogeneous.
Investigate Q2:114 places-of-worship historical context without assigning a specific incident unsupported by the verse.
Design a substantive religious-claims dossier with explicit Q2:115–116 links only after primary text verification.
